source_quotes.uky: Univ. of Kentucky Entomology, ENTFACT-609 Clothes Moths: Clothes moth adults do not feed so they cause no injury to fabrics. However, the adults lay about 40-50 pinhead-sized eggs on vulnerable substrates, which in turn, hatch into the fabric-eating larvae. / Articles commonly infested include sweaters, scarves, coats, blankets, rugs... / The larvae prefer to feed in dark, undisturbed areas such as closets.
source_quotes.ucipm: UC IPM Pest Notes: Clothes Moths (Pub. 7435): Fabrics with food, perspiration, or urine stains are more subject to damage. / insects are less likely to feed on clean fabrics than on heavily soiled ones. / enclosing the item in a plastic bag and placing it in a freezer for several days at temperatures lower than 18°F. / these moths are weak flyers that aren't attracted to lights.
